name: Sport or physical skill
description: Learn or sharpen a physical skill (a swimming stroke, climbing, a tennis serve, skating, a martial art...): fundamentals, drills, conditioning, video feedback and a test to see your progress.

steps.title: Safety, equipment and baseline test
steps.description: Get the right gear, check with a doctor if needed and record where you are now: a simple test you can repeat later.

steps.title: Fundamentals and body position
steps.description: Learn the basic stance, grip or posture of the skill with a coach, a good video course or a training partner.

steps.title: Core movement drills
steps.description: Break the skill into its simplest movements and repeat each one slowly and cleanly before adding speed or power.

steps.title: Conditioning: strength, mobility and endurance
steps.description: Build the physical base the skill needs, with a progressive plan of two or three sessions a week.

steps.title: Put the pieces together
steps.description: Combine the drills into the full movement, first slowly and then at normal pace, keeping the technique intact.

steps.title: Video your technique and review it
steps.description: Film yourself from two angles, compare with a reference and ask a coach or an experienced practitioner for feedback.

steps.title: Skill under pressure
steps.description: Use the skill in games, routes, sets, sparring or timed attempts, where fatigue and opponents test it.

steps.title: Recovery and injury prevention routine
steps.description: Add stretching, mobility, sleep and rest days. Learn the warning signs that tell you to stop.

steps.title: Retest and set the next level
steps.description: Repeat your baseline test, compare, celebrate the progress and choose the next target.

competencies.name: Technique
competencies.description: Correct, repeatable movement of the skill at normal pace.

competencies.name: Conditioning
competencies.description: The strength, endurance and speed the skill demands.

competencies.name: Performance under pressure
competencies.description: Keeping your technique when you are tired, nervous or competing.

competencies.name: Mobility and injury prevention
competencies.description: Range of motion, warm-up and recovery habits that keep you training.

competencies.name: Tactics and game sense
competencies.description: Reading the situation and choosing the right action.

cards.back: Gradually increasing the demand of training (load, volume, speed or difficulty) so the body keeps adapting.

cards.front: What does the RPE scale measure?
cards.back: Rating of perceived exertion, from 1 (very easy) to 10 (maximum effort). It tells you how hard a session felt.
It raises body temperature and heart rate, lubricates the joints and rehearses the movements, lowering the risk of injury and improving performance.
What you feel and what you do often differ. Video shows the real movement and lets you compare it with a reference.
Training focused on a specific weakness, slightly beyond your current ability, with immediate feedback and full attention.

cards.front: Why are rest days part of training?
cards.back: The body adapts during recovery, not during the session. Plan at least one or two rest days a week and sleep enough.

cards.front: What is delayed onset muscle soreness?
cards.back: Muscle ache that peaks one or two days after unfamiliar effort. It is normal and passes; sharp or joint pain is not, so stop and get it checked.
